target_customer: Aspiring homebuyers in Vietnam and Southeast Asia who cannot get or afford bank mortgages, plus investors who co-fund purchases.
problem: Bank mortgages in the region carry high interest (12 percent or more per the YC page), strict documentation and large deposits, which locks out many would be owners.
business_model: Rent-to-own and co-investment real estate financing: Homebase buys the home, the client pays a deposit and monthly payments and later buys out its share; investor product earns monthly returns

founders.name: Phillip An
founders.background_notes: Quoted as co-founder and COO in TechCrunch, Nov 2021.

founders.name: Hung Doan
founders.background_notes: Named among founders in an April 2020 e27 interview.

founders.background_notes: Named among founders in an April 2020 e27 interview.

competitors.what: US rent-to-own model that inspired Homebase; not a regional competitor

competitors.name: ZeroDown
competitors.what: US rent-to-own model that inspired Homebase; not a regional competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly financial structuring, underwriting and operations on top of standard software; the hard parts were legal structure for property ownership and capital sourcing rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The structure was copyable, though local legal know how, developer partnerships and access to cheap capital gave some friction. Dependence on a weak property market hurt it later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows banks copying the product; the bigger pressure was Vietnam's 2022 to 2025 real estate downturn.

market_need_then: The founders interviewed over 70 customers and cited a broken home financing system with mortgage rates of 12 percent or more and heavy documentation, in a market with a young, urbanizing population.

branding.domain_note: gethomebase.com now redirects to homebase.com.vn; the exact homebase.com belongs to an unrelated company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Empathetic and aspirational: 'making the dream of home ownership come true' (site tagline in Vietnamese).

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Vietcetera, Forbes Vietnam, Vietnam Investment Review and Tech in Asia per its own site; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press and awards (Plug and Play 2020, KPMG and HSBC 2022 per its own site) but a very generic name shared with an HR software company and a property tax product, so search and recall were weak.

pivots.to: HR technology platform launched by the founder
pivots.why: DealStreetAsia headline ties it to a weak Vietnamese real estate market; the article body was paywalled.

outcome_analysis: Homebase raised a 30 million dollar equity and debt round in November 2021 on a rent-to-own model adapted from Divvy Homes and ZeroDown, operating in Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Da Nang. The Vietnamese property market then weakened, peers like Propzy wound down, and in March 2025 DealStreetAsia reported the founder moving into an HR tech platform, while the financing website still operates. The directory status is Active, so it is stalled rather than shut down, and the cause of the shift is inferred from a headline.
notes: The 30 million dollar figure is equity plus debt with no disclosed split (TechCrunch, cross checked with Vietstock and VnExpress headlines). Seedtable lists about 100 million across two rounds including a 70 million Series C and CB Insights lists a 200 thousand dollar 2025 seed; both are unverified and probably wrong or a different company. The December 2020 round is only described as seven figures in USD, so amount is null. The stage 'other' is used for the 2020 pre Series A and 2021 round because sources do not label them reliably. The funding round TechCrunch article quotes only Phillip An and does not name Jun Yuan Tan. Competition lists only the US models named in 2020 coverage; no regional competitors were named.
